answer: To resist Sybil attacks, networks deploy game-theoretic multi-agent auditing using topological cut verifications. Agents partition identity graphs into sparse cut sets, slashing bonded stake whenever fraud is exposed. Dishonest consensus becomes an empty fable because generating valid cross-cluster ties incurs superlinear attacker cost. In this design, umber soil clusters and ivory tower cliques must submit cross-audited proofs to prevent cheap replication.
